data.name: Muscles_intent
data.intent_description: Question about how to become muscular and which exercises to perform.

bodies.name: Focus on heavy compound lifts like squats, deadlifts, bench press, overhead press, and rows to build overall muscle mass.
Train 3–5 times per week, progressively increasing the weight while eating enough protein and calories to support growth.
Get good sleep and stay consistent—muscle comes from steady effort over time.
Hi, I am your buddy, the fitness agent.
Nutrition basics: Eat mostly whole foods (lean protein, vegetables, fruits, whole grains, healthy fats). Protein: ~1.6–2.2 g per kg of body weight daily..
Match calories to your goal: slight surplus to gain muscle, deficit to lose fat, maintenance to stay the same.
Carbs fuel training; fats support hormones.
Drink plenty of water and limit ultra-processed foods and alcohol.
Be consistent — results come from habits, not perfection

bodies.name: Focus on big, heavy lifts to build muscle: squats, deadlifts, bench press, overhead press, and rows.
Train 3–5 days a week. Add a little weight over time. Eat enough protein and calories to grow.
Sleep well and be consistent. Muscle grows with steady effort over time.
Eat mostly whole foods: lean protein, vegetables, fruit, whole grains, and healthy fats. Aim for 1.6 to 2.2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight each day.
Match calories to your goal: eat a little more to gain muscle, eat less to lose fat, eat the same to stay the same.
Carbs give you energy for training. Fats help your hormones.
Drink plenty of water. Limit highly processed foods and alcohol.
Be consistent. Results come from good habits, not perfection.

bodies.name: Hi, I am your buddy, the fitness agent.
I am here to answer any questions regarding exercises, nutrition and recovery.

fallbackBodies.name: I focus on gym and fitness topics only dude.

bodies.name: Focus on accessible compound upper-body and core movements like bench press or machine chest press, overhead press, seated rows, lat pulldowns/assisted pull-ups, dips or triceps pushdowns, face pulls, and anti-rotation core work (e.g., Pallof press), using seated or strap-stabilized setups as needed.

Train 3–5 times per week, progressively increasing resistance on upper-body and core-focused exercises while eating enough protein and calories to support growth; balance pushing and pulling to protect your shoulders and allow adequate recovery.
Get good sleep and stay consistent—muscle comes from steady effort over time.
Nutrition basics: Eat mostly whole foods (lean protein, vegetables, fruits, whole grains, healthy fats). Protein: ~1.6–2.2 g per kg of body weight daily..
Match calories to your goal: slight surplus to gain muscle, deficit to lose fat, maintenance to stay the same.
Carbs fuel training; fats support hormones.
Drink plenty of water and limit ultra-processed foods and alcohol.
Be consistent — results come from habits, not perfection
AI response 🪄
